events.text: On a mountain pass, a dozen bandits step onto the road. Their leader grins. 'Toll's everything you have. Including the boots.'

ok.log: When it is over, the bandits are running and their leader is not. You take the toll money back, plus interest.

fail.log: There are too many. You wake in a ditch, robbed of everything, including the boots.

effects.log: You hand over everything. The leader pats your cheek. 'Smart. Smart ones live long.'

ok.log: You slide down a scree slope that no sane bandit would follow.

fail.log: The slope is steeper than it looked. You break two ribs, but you are free.

choices.text: (I remember this) Take the goat trail around the pass

effects.log: A feeling older than memory says where the bandits wait. You take the goat trail and pass them unseen, waving politely from a ridge.
effects.logPast: You remember this ambush from a life that ended here. You take the goat trail and pass the bandits unseen, waving politely from a ridge.

variants: A dozen bandits block the mountain pass. Their leader grins. 'The toll is everything you own. Boots too.'

events.text: A plague comes up the river with the rice boats. By autumn, half the houses on your street have a white cloth on the door.

ok.log: You sleep in a cave until the first snow. When you come back, the town is quieter. Much quieter.

fail.log: The fever finds you anyway, in the hills, alone. You survive it. Barely.

ok.log: You carry water and bury the dead for three months. People remember who stayed.

fail.log: You catch it in the second month. Strangers you once nursed nurse you now.

variants: Sickness comes upriver on the rice barges. By the end of summer, white cloths hang on half the doors of your street.
The boats from downriver bring a fever with them. Within a season, every other house on your lane has a white cloth on its door.

events.text: At a roadside inn, the tea tastes faintly of almonds. The waiter is suddenly very interested in the ceiling.

choices.text: Force the poison out with internal energy

ok.log: You circulate your energy and sweat the poison out through your fingertips. The waiter is already gone.

fail.deathCause: poison that never left your blood
fail.log: You get most of it out. Most.

choices.text: Throw up and chase the waiter

ok.log: You catch him in the stables. He was paid by a man in a bamboo hat. He never saw the face.

fail.log: You make it three steps before your legs give out. A doctor finds you just in time.

effects.log: You swallow the antidote. It tastes worse than the poison. It works.

choices.text: (I remember this) Swap cups with the waiter

effects.log: Something about this tea sets your teeth on edge. You swap the cups while he looks at the ceiling. He drinks. He does not enjoy it.
effects.logPast: In another life, this tea killed you. This time you swap the cups while he looks at the ceiling. He drinks. He does not enjoy it.

effects.log: The poison goes through you like water through a sieve. You feel slightly warm. Everyone watching feels slightly afraid.

choices.text: Lie down and drink water until it passes

effects.log: You stagger to a back room and drink jug after jug of water while the ceiling spins. It passes, slowly, over two days. The waiter is long gone, and so is your strength for a while.

variants: The tea at the roadside inn has a faint taste of bitter almonds. The waiter suddenly finds the rafters fascinating.

events.text: A seventeen-year-old in a spotless white robe walks into the teahouse and points his sword at you. 'You are famous. After today, I will be.'

ok.log: It takes three moves. He leaves with a bruise and, you hope, some humility.

fail.log: It takes three moves. They are his. The whole teahouse saw.

choices.text: Tell him to come back in ten years

effects.log: He goes red and storms out. You suspect you will see him again.

ok.log: By the third pot, he is telling you about his mother. By the fourth, he wants to be your disciple.

fail.log: He throws the tea in your face, then the teapot, then himself.

variants: A youth of seventeen in a spotless white robe marches into the teahouse and levels his sword at you. 'You are famous. After today, I will be.'

events.text: You wake at the third watch. Someone is standing at the foot of your bed, perfectly still, holding a needle that catches the moonlight.

ok.log: Your palm lands first. The assassin goes through the window. There is a tattoo of a black lotus on the wrist.

fail.log: The needle finds your shoulder instead of your throat. The assassin is gone before you can scream.

ok.log: A long, long minute. Then the figure leaves. In the morning there is a black lotus on your pillow. A warning.

fail.log: It was not a warning. You wake up two days later, alive only because the poison was old.

choices.text: (I remember this) Roll aside before the needle falls

effects.log: A chill you cannot name says the needle is coming. You are already moving when it drops, and your counter-palm sends the assassin fleeing into the night.
effects.logPast: You have died in this bed before. This time you are already moving when the needle drops, and your counter-palm sends the assassin fleeing into the night.

events.text: Red banners on the horizon. The Demonic Cult is raiding the valley, and the Orthodox Alliance is three days away.

ok.log: You hold the bridge until dawn. When the Alliance finally arrives, they find you asleep on a pile of red banners.

fail.log: You hold the bridge for an hour. It is enough for the children to escape. It is nearly the end of you.

choices.text: Get the villagers into the mountains

ok.log: You lead forty people over a goat path in the dark. Every one of them makes it.

fail.log: Panic. People scatter. You save who you can.

effects.log: You hide in the grain cellar and listen. You will hear it for years.

choices.text: (I remember this) You warned the village last spring

effects.log: You remembered the red banners from a past life, so the village had walls, traps and an escape path ready. The Cult finds nothing but an empty valley and a very rude welcome.

events.text: Gathering firewood at dusk, you realise the orange rock in the bamboo has been breathing this whole time.

ok.log: The tiger considers you, decides you are too loud to be worth it, and leaves.

fail.deathCause: a tiger in the bamboo forest
fail.log: The tiger does not care how tall you are. You escape up a tree, bleeding.

ok.log: You kill a tiger with your bare hands. You will never, ever stop telling this story.

fail.deathCause: a tiger in the bamboo forest
fail.log: You lose. Luckily, so does the tiger's interest. A woodcutter finds you.

events.text: The harvest fails. By midwinter, people are boiling tree bark and belts.

choices.text: Share what you have (30 taels of rice)

effects.log: You go hungry so a family down the road does not. You are thin by spring, and not sorry.

ok.log: You bring back a frozen deer. The whole street eats for a week.

fail.deathCause: the cold of a hungry winter
fail.log: The mountain takes two of your toes and nearly the rest of you.

effects.log: You survive the winter on rice-water and stubbornness.

events.text: War between the sects. {sect} calls every disciple to the front. The elders do not ask. They tell.

ok.log: Three months of mud and blood. You come home with a scar across your face and a name people whisper.

fail.log: You are carried off the field on a door. The war ends without you.

effects.log: You carry rice and bandages for a season. Less glory. More of you left.
You slip away. By morning you are a wanderer with no sect and a price on your head, a small one.

events.text: Your face is on a wanted poster at the crossroads. The drawing is terrible. The reward is not.

choices.text: Tear it down and move on

ok.log: No one recognises you. The drawing really is terrible.

fail.log: Three bounty hunters recognise you anyway. You get away, carrying one of their arrows.

ok.log: You find the bounty hunters' camp before they find you. You keep their silver.

fail.log: They were waiting for exactly that.

events.text: A wild-haired old man is screaming at a tree on the roadside. His eyes are red from qi deviation. He turns to you, and the tree behind him falls over.

ok.log: He goes back to screaming at the tree stump. You walk very quickly for a very long time.

fail.log: He hits you once, apologises, and hits you again.

ok.log: You press your palm to his back and guide his energy home. He weeps, and teaches you a breathing trick from sixty years ago.

fail.log: His qi floods into your meridians like a river through a paper wall.

events.text: The river breaks its banks in the night. You wake to water at your bed.

ok.log: Two days on the roof, eating a wet cabbage. You lose most of what you own, but not yourself.

fail.log: The current takes you a mile before a tree catches you. The tree is the only reason you are alive.

ok.log: You get all four of them out. Their mother still sends you rice cakes every New Year.

fail.log: You get them out. The water nearly does not let you follow.

choices.text: Let everything go and ride the door out

effects.log: You tear the door off its hinges and ride it into the dark. By dawn you are on a hillside a mile away, cold and bruised, and everything you owned is somewhere in the river.

variants: In the night the river comes over its banks. You wake with water lapping at your bed.
A roar in the dark, then the cold: the river has broken through, and water is already rising around your bed.

events.text: A man in a very clean robe sells you a map to the tomb of a legendary sword master. Only 50 taels. He has, he says, just the one.

choices.text: Buy it and follow the map

ok.log: The tomb is fake. The map is fake. But the cave it leads to has a real bandit stash in it. You feel this counts.

fail.log: The map leads to a cliff, a wasp nest, and the realisation that he had a whole bag of the maps.

ok.log: His story changes three times in one breath. You wish him a good day. He does not have one: the guards were listening.

fail.log: His answer is so moving that you buy two.

effects.log: You walk away. The next customer buys four.
You remember this man, and the bag of maps. The guards find forty-one of them. They give you a reward. He gives you a look.

variants: A man in a suspiciously clean robe offers you a map to the tomb of a legendary sword master. Only 50 taels. It is, he swears, the only one.

events.text: Reaching for a herb under a rock, you feel two tiny, precise pricks on your wrist.

ok.log: Disgusting. Effective. You are fine, give or take a swollen arm.

fail.log: Your arm swells to twice its size. You spend a week in a fever, talking to your ancestors.

effects.log: The antidote works. You make a mental note: look under rocks with a stick.
The poison goes through you like water through a sieve. You feel slightly warm. Everyone watching feels slightly afraid.

events.text: You bump into a young master in the market. His tea spills. His four bodyguards put their hands on their swords. 'Kneel,' he says, 'and I will only break a hand.'

effects.log: You kneel. He laughs and walks away. You burn the memory into your bones.

ok.log: Five against one. When it is over, the young master is the one kneeling. The market applauds.

fail.log: There were five of them. There were always going to be five of them.

ok.log: You praise his robe, his sword, and his father. He decides you are not worth the effort.

fail.log: Your praise sounds exactly as sarcastic as it was. The bodyguards teach you a lesson.

variants: You jostle a young master in the market and his tea goes everywhere. Four bodyguards reach for their swords. 'Kneel,' he says, 'and I will only break a hand.'

events.text: The old poison stirs in your blood again. Your hands go numb every morning now.

effects.log: The healer needles you for a week and charges you a fortune. The numbness is gone.

choices.text: Press it down with internal energy

ok.log: You press the poison back into the corner of your body where it lives. For now.

fail.deathCause: poison that never left your blood
fail.log: The poison wins this round. You spend the season in bed.

events.text: A rumble on the mountain road. You look up. Half the mountain is coming down to meet you.

ok.log: You outrun a mountain. You sit in the dust afterwards and laugh until you cough.

fail.deathCause: a rockslide on the mountain road
fail.log: A boulder clips you. You dig yourself out after an hour, with a new appreciation for being alive.

choices.text: Use lightness technique across the falling rocks

ok.log: You run up the falling rocks like stairs. A passing merchant tells the story in every town for a year.

fail.deathCause: a rockslide on the mountain road
fail.log: One of the stairs was not a stair.

choices.text: (I remember this) Take the lower path today

effects.log: Something in your bones says this mountain will move. You take the lower path and watch the rockslide from a safe distance, eating a rice ball.
effects.logPast: You remember this mountain coming down on you. You take the lower path and watch the rockslide from a safe distance, eating a rice ball.
